narrative:
The model determined that you have a 33% chance of being a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the status of your checking account, how long you have been employed, and the amount in your savings. Your checking account status had the strongest influence and actually worked in your favor because you have no checking account. Among approved applicants, 59% also have no checking account, so this is quite common. However, your unemployment status pushed the decision strongly toward denial. Only 7% of approved applicants are unemployed, making this a significant negative factor. Your low savings balance of less than 100 DM also nudged the prediction toward bad credit risk, though less strongly. Many approved applicants (46%) have similarly low savings, but combined with your employment situation it added to the concern.

In short, while your clean checking account history helped your case, the combination of being unemployed and having very limited savings outweighed that positive and led to the denial.

You should focus on securing stable employment and building up your savings before reapplying. This would likely improve your chances significantly with the bank. (198 words)
